The City of Bellingham solicits interest from consulting firms with expertise in Civil and Structural Engineering Design. This agreement will be for approximately two years in duration, beginning October 2026 and ending October 2028, with the option for the City of Bellingham to extend it for additional time and money if necessary.  Consultants will be considered for the following project.

 

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses.

Project Description

The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of preparing preliminary engineering design for the Electric Avenue- Whatcom Creek Replacement project. The proposed improvements include replacing the existing four span reinforced concrete structure with an approximately 105 foot long single span prestressed concrete girder structure. This includes widening the existing bridge deck to accommodate two travel lanes, five-foot bike lanes in both directions, and six-foot pedestrian walkways on both sides with ADA compliant approaches. Utilities on the existing bridge will need to be maintained in service during and after construction. This project has a 0% FSBE goal with a 10% SBE voluntary goal. The major features of the project are as follows:

 

·       Roadway, bicycle and pedestrian improvements on new bridge and approaches
·       Structural design for the new bridge structure
·       Utility design for new bridge and temporary utility bypass during construction
·       Environmental documentation and preparation of permit applications, including NEPA

 

Consultants shall have expertise in the following:

·       Traffic control measures and methodologies (in accordance with the MUTCD) to complete the project as one along with accommodation to multi-modal uses
·       WSDOT Local Programs requirements for Federally Funded projects including WSDOT Local Agency Guidelines (LAG) Manual
·       FSBE/SBE approach and commitment
·       MUTCD, NACTO, and AASHTO standards
·       City of Bellingham Development Guidelines and Improvement Standards, and the Bellingham Municipal Code
·       City of Bellingham and Department of Ecology standards for storm water management, per the most recently adopted version of the SWMMWW.
·       ADA Requirements
·       Shoreline Design
·       Local, State (Including HPA), and Federal Permitting Requirements

 

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to retain the services of the successful firm(s) for any subsequent phases (Right of Way, Construction) associated with these projects.

 

All prospective consultants are advised that federally funded projects will be held to Federal EEO requirements.

 

 

Evaluation Criteria                                                                      100 Points Total

Submittals will be evaluated and ranked based on the following criteria:

1.   Qualification of Proposed Project Manager                             15 points
2.   Qualifications of Key Personnel/Expertise of Firm                 15 points
3.   Ability to meet schedule                                                          15 points
4.   Approach to project                                                                 20 points
5.   Familiarity with WSDOT/FHWA/Environmental standards  15 points
6.   Past Performance/References                                                  10 points
7.   FSBE/SBE Approach and Commitment                                  5 points
8.   Approach to Construction Management                                  5 points

 

Submittal

All submittals shall include a signed cover letter including the following information: Firm name, phone, fax numbers, email; Name of Principal-in-Charge and Project Manager; and Number of employees in each firm proposed to project. Additional project information is included in the supplemental information which can be found at https://cob.procureware.com/home. Submittal Information Forms for each Prime and Subconsultant listed in submittal should be included on WSDOT Form 140-565 and Form 140-566, respectively.

 

Submittals shall be limited to a maximum of ten 8-1/2" by 11" pages (ten single-sided or five pages double-sided), not including the title page (limited to one page), table of contents (limited to one page), resumes (limited to one page for each individual) and forms 140-565 and 140-566 (limited to one per company). Submittals over the maximum page size limit will not be considered.

 

The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFQ by submitting their Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/ no later than 11:00 a.m. on August 4, 2026.  Submittals will not be accepted after that time and date.  Any questions regarding this project should be directed to City Purchasing Department, at (360) 778-7750 or email: bids@cob.org

The City of Bellingham is soliciting proposals from qualified consulting firms to provide mitigation monitoring and reporting services under a five-year contract, with the option of a mutually agreed-upon two-year extension.


The City of Bellingham Public Works Department’s Mitigation Program manages the maintenance and monitoring of permittee-responsible compensatory mitigation sites resulting from Public Works Department capital construction projects. The mitigation compensates for wetland, stream, and/or buffer impacts. Maintenance and monitoring are unique to each site and defined by the site’s specific regulatory permits. Maintenance and monitoring help achieve compliance with performance standards established in each site’s regulatory permits.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking submittals (Invitation No. 2B-2023) from engineering firms interested in providing professional design services to the Engineering Division of the Public Works Department for the Tremont Lift Station Design (EU-0193).
A sewer system was built in 2010 along Meridian St. (SR 539) within the Urban Growth Area (UGA) to accommodate growth from Van Wyck Rd. to Smith Rd. It also accommodates properties along the side roads of Kline Road and Kelly Road. A new Lift Station is required to connect this system to the City of Bellingham sewer system. CITY OF BELLINGHAM 

RFP 32B-2026  

Annual Confined Space Standby-Rescue Services 

The purpose of this Request for Proposal (RFP) is to solicit proposals, through a competitive process, for confined space standby rescue services during Permit-Required Confined Space (PRCS) entries performed by District personnel and/or its contractors and consultants on an on-call or an “as needed” basis.  

All services shall comply with applicable federal and Washington State regulations, including OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 (Permit-Required Confined Spaces) and Washington Administrative Code (WAC) Chapter 296-809 (Confined Spaces). 

The City of Bellingham Plants Division utilizes a variety of tanks for different purposes, ranging from wastewater mixing to potable water storage. When these tanks are entered, it is often necessary for multiple personnel to work inside simultaneously. Due to the number of workers involved, as well as the size and configuration of many of these tanks, the use of individual tethered confined-space retrieval systems is often impractical and may hinder the safe and efficient completion of the work. 

The Plants Division typically performs around 10 tank-entry projects annually, although the actual number may vary from year to year depending on operational and maintenance needs. Some of these projects may require confined-space entry for one to three consecutive days. 

 The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFP by submitting their electronic proposal. Interested parties may view the solicitation documents on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing bids email at bids@cob.org

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to provide architectural/engineering and related services.

 

This work includes all services related to building and bridge structure repair, replacement, or renovation of any building, structure, or bridge in the Park’s system include design, permitting, or construction administration.

 

While the focus of this work is to provide all services necessary or related to structures, other services may be needed in coordination with this work such as utilities, environmental permitting/reporting/mitigation. Work may also include construction administration support.

 

For efficiency in contracting and project management, the City is issuing one RFQ for this general work. Various contracts will be negotiated for each project on an as-needed basis for the duration of services up to 3 years, which could be extended for projects that are already contracted and underway under this RFQ. It is the City’s intent to contract with only one consultant team with all the support services needed to carry out these various projects, which may also include daily inspections and construction administration support using City and WSDOT inspection forms and the WSDOT construction manual.

RFQ 30B-2026

Downtown Signalized Intersection Accessibility and Safety Improvements Project ET037-Federal Aid Project-00S(748)

The City of Bellingham solicits interest from consulting firms with expertise in Civil Design. This agreement will be for approximately seven months in duration, beginning September 2026 and ending March 2027, with the option for the City of Bellingham to extend it for additional time and money if necessary.  Consultants will be considered for the following federally funded project. 



The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses. 



Project Description 

The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of preparing preliminary engineering design for Downtown Signalized Intersection Accessibility and Safety Improvements Project. The project will improve signals and related infrastructure at three downtown intersections, including the intersections of Railroad Ave. with Magnolia St., Holly St., and Chestnut St. This project has a 0% FSBE goal with a 10% SBE voluntary goal. The major features of the project are as follows: 



Signal Reconstruction 

Install Curb Extensions 

ADA Improvements 

Related Utility Modifications 



Other features of the project are as follows: 

Collect Survey data for the areas shown within the project vicinity map. 

Assess permitting needs, perform environmental reporting as needed and assist the City in acquiring necessary permits for CN obligation (i.e. NEPA, cultural resources, etc.).  

Prepare complete bid documents including construction plans, technical specifications, and engineers estimate (PS&E). 

Other work that may be included, depending on project funding or as part of future amendments: 

Services during bidding 

Services during construction 



The City of Bellingham reserves the right to retain the services of the successful firm(s) for any subsequent phases (R/W, CN, Construction Management) associated with these projects. 



All prospective consultants are advised that federally funded projects will be held to Federal EEO requirements. 



Evaluation Criteria 100 Points Total 

Submittals will be evaluated and ranked based on the following criteria: 

Qualification of Proposed Project Manager 15 points 

Qualifications of Key Personnel/Expertise of Firm  15 points 

Ability to meet schedule 20 points 

Approach to project 20 points 

Familiarity with WSDOT/FHWA standards 15 points 

Past Performance/References 5 points 

FSBE/SBE Approach and Commitment 5 points 

Approach to Construction Management (Construction Phase) 5 points 



Submittal 

All submittals shall include a signed cover letter including the following information: Firm name, phone, fax numbers, email; Name of Principal-in-Charge and Project Manager; and Number of employees in each firm proposed to project. Additional project information is included in the supplemental information which can be found at https://cob.procureware.com/home. Submittal Information Forms for each Prime and Subconsultant listed in submittal should be included on WSDOT Form 140-565 and Form 140-566, respectively. 



Submittals shall be limited to a maximum of ten 8-1/2" by 11" pages (ten single-sided or five pages double-sided), not including the title page (limited to one page), table of contents (limited to one page), resumes (limited to one page for each individual) and forms 140-565 and 140-566 (limited to one per company). Submittals over the maximum page size limit will not be considered.  



The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFQ by submitting their Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/  no later than 11:00 a.m. on June 23, 2026.  Submittals will not be accepted after that time and date.  Any questions regarding this project should be directed to City Purchasing Department, at (360) 778-7750 or email: bids@cob.org  



Estimated Procurement Schedule 

These dates are estimates and subject to change by the City. 

Advertise RFQ  June 2 & June 9, 2026 

Deadline for questions  June 16, 2026 

Receive SOQs June 23, 2026 

Review and Rank SOQs July 6, 2026 

Consultant Selection Interviews July 18, 2026 

Consultant Selection/Award July 21, 2026 

Scoping and Contract August 2026 

Begin Work September 2026 

Complete Work/End Contract March 2027 



Contract Type 

Contract type (method of payment) will be Negotiated Hourly Rate utilizing WSDOT’s Local Agency A&E Professional Services Negotiated Hourly Rate Consultant Agreement.  Submission of cost proposal or elements of cost shall not be submitted until a consultant selection has been made. 



The Consultant(s) awarded the contract will be required to obtain and maintain a City of Bellingham Business License. 



Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Information 

The City of Bellingham in accordance with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (Section 504) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), commits to nondiscrimination on the basis of disability, in all of its programs and activities. This material can be made available in an alternate format by emailing Holly Pederson, City of Bellingham ADA Coordinator at hdpederson@cob.org or by calling collect (360) 778-7950.   



Title VI Statement 

The City of Bellingham, in accordance with the provisions of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (78 Stat. 252, 42 U.S.C. 2000d to 2000d-4) and the Regulations, hereby notifies all bidders that it will affirmatively ensure that in any contract entered into pursuant to this advertisement, disadvantaged business enterprises will be afforded full and fair opportunity to submit bids in response to this invitation and will not be discriminated against on the grounds of race, color, or national origin in consideration for an award. 



Dates of publication in the Cascadia Daily, the Daily Journal of Commerce, and Office of Minority and Women’s Business Enterprises (OMWBE): June 2, 2026, and June 9, 2026.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 36B-2023) from consulting firms interested in providing professional consulting services for the Raw Water Intake – Condition Assessment and Inter-tie Design Project (City Project Number EW241). 

The project will include a condition assessment for various facilities conveying raw water from the Lake Whatcom Reservoir to the City Water Treatment Plant.  This municipal owned water treatment facility operates 24hrs per day and is critical City infrastructure.  The Condition Assessment of the Raw Water Intake system will involve field inspection and documentation of: 72-inch submerged Intake Pipeline, Gatehouse, Intake Tunnel and Screenhouse.  The Condition Assessment of the Old Mill Intake system will involve field inspection and documentation of: 48-inch submerged Intake Pipeline, Shore structure, Brick tunnel, Old Larson facility, and 30/24-inch conveyance piping.  All inspections will require coordination for facility shutdown.  Some elements of the fieldwork are expected to require diving and remote-operated submersible units. The project will also include hydraulic analysis of the Old Mill Intake System, and the design and permitting of an Inter-tie pipeline system between the Old Mill Intake and the Raw Water Intake Systems.
Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham sewer utility funds.

The work consists of: removal rocks and debris from the inlet channel at the Post Point Waste Water Treatment Facility to the bar screens to a depth of three (3) feet below the level of the bar screen channel and deposit the rocks and debris into a container for transport to an approved disposal site. The channel is approximately 6’ wide by 50’ long.

The improvement consists of: In-water construction to improve fish passage at the Middle Fork Nooksack river, including partial demolition of the City’s diversion dam structure, and restoration of approximately 500 linear feet of river channel. Project work also includes facility construction of an automated municipal water supply diversion intake system, including an in-water intake structure, fish screening facility, conveyance piping, and modifications to the existing diversion facility at the site.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to provide Structural Analysis of the Commercial Street Parking Garage services. This structure is located at 1300 Commercial Street in the heart of the downtown shopping district.  The structure is comprised of five levels with the ground floor level housing several businesses along Commercial Street and W. Holly Street. The plaza off Commercial Street includes two non-ADA compliant restrooms and is an area where markets and events are conducted.

 

The building was originally constructed in 1969. It is a cast in place post tensioned  joist garage consisting of one below grade parking area, retail on the ground level on the south and west frontages of the structure. The garage was built with three elevated parking desks. In 1992 a mezzanine accessible from the alley was built using steel framing with composite concrete decking. The addition also extended the existing concrete shear walls and spiral ramp up to the fifth-floor level.  The garage lateral system consists of concrete shear walls down the middle of the building, interior transverse walls near the ends, around the stair towers and the circular ramp walls. The building originally had precast concrete cladding panels on all sides of the structure. The panels were removed from the Commercial Street and Holly Street sides several years ago and it is the City’s intention to remove the panels on the remaining two sides. The structure has two enclosed stairwells centered on the perimeter of the northwest and southeast sides of the building and the four upper levels are served by a single 5 stop passenger elevator rated for 2,500 lbs. The elevator cab and electronics were replaced in 2011 and the lighting was upgraded in 2012. There were windows installed in the exterior stairwells in 2016.

The City of Bellingham has traditionally set speed limits based upon standards and guidance within the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) as revised by the Washington Administrative Code (WAC) 468-95-045. That guidance recommends evaluation of many factors, the primary of which is the prevailing 85th percentile speed. Many agencies, including Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) are looking to revise their policies and practices regarding speed limit setting to have the goal of injury minimization in the event of crashes in adherence to agency “Vision Zero” goals and/or utilization of Safe Systems approaches. In response to this movement there are many different methods that are being considered to achieve these end goals, including the development of a city-wide speed limit setting policy that is based on current engineering best practices.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is soliciting for Statements of Qualifications (SOQs) from consulting firms or teams interested in providing professional assessment and design services for the Water Quality Infrastructure Prioritization Assessment Project (the “Project”).
Project Objective:
The Project will collect and analyze water quality data in order to identify, prioritize, conceptualize, and/or engineer stormwater management actions (SMAs) that maximize protection of the City’s waterways from impacts of urbanization. This project consists of basin mapping, study development, field research, data analysis, report writing, and professional consulting related to engineering/design of water quality facilities or other non-structural SMAs.
Using existing data, maps, and studies, the chosen consultant will characterize water quality conditions in six freshwater watersheds as well as areas inside Bellingham city limits which drain to marine waters. Then, the consultant will develop a tool, in partnership with city staff, that can be calibrated to predict real-world water quality parameters based on a multitude of inputs from existing data. Through field research in partnership with the City’s water quality laboratory, the consultant will then analyze real-world pollutant concentrations in stormwater runoff as it enters and moves through the City of Bellingham’s stormwater infrastructure and into creeks and marine waters. The intent of this sampling, conducted over at least two years, will be to calibrate the predictive tool. At the completion of the field research, the consultant will produce a matrix of SMAs and provide conceptual-level design work and/or feasibility analysis for up to ten actions prioritized by the City for further consideration.
Ideally, the consultant’s scope for this project will align closely to tasks 2, 3, and 4 as detailed in the City’s funding agreement with the Department of Ecology, attached for reference. A full and detailed scope of work will be negotiated with the chosen consultant after selection.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications from engineering consulting firms with expertise in the design and permitting of environmental cleanup projects at sites with contaminated soil and groundwater. 

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 47B-2024) from engineering and environmental consulting firms interested in providing professional consulting services for the McKenzie Street Contaminated Site Cleanup Project, City Project Number EU198.

 

The parcel of 200 & 210 McKenzie Avenue is in Bellingham, WA within the Fairhaven Neighborhood. The parcel is adjacent to the Post Point Wastewater Treatment Plant, which lies to the southwest. The buildings on the parcel currently house storage and facilities for the Treatment Plant and a plastic boat builder.  Since 1904, the property has been used for plastic and fiberglass boat manufacturing, as well as various metal forging and fabrication operations. Petroleum storage tanks were present on the property from 1904 to the 1980s. Heavy metals, arsenic, lead, and petroleum contamination have been identified at the site through groundwater monitoring; and layers of metal waste, broken glass, and refuse were found in the soils through the excavation of test pits. More information on the history of the site and nature of the pollutants can be found in Attachment C, Remedial Investigation and Feasibility Study (RIFS) completed for the City by All4, LLC, which was most recently revised on May 17, 2024.

 

As the city intends to use this property to allow for future expansion of the Post Point Wastewater Treatment Plant, remediation of the site is required for the safety of our community and to adhere with local, state, and federal requirements. Section 3.6 of the RIFS details potential alternatives to the remediation, the City’s preliminary choice is Alternative 1. The City requests assistance in determining those requirements and relevant regulations and obtaining permits needed to complete the remediation work. This contract will include preparation of bid-ready documents to perform the remediation work. Funding will be from the City’s sewer fund.

 

Services, including professional engineering services, permitting development, public outreach, cultural resource consultation, construction engineering and/or administration, and long-term site monitoring support may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham sewer utility funds.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications (SOQ) from consulting firms with expertise in municipal utility design and rehabilitation.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 77B-2025) from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the King Mountain Reservoir project (EW247) project.

 

Project Description

 

The King Mountain Reservoir project aims to satisfy the long-term water system storage needs for a large portion of the City potable water system. The City’s water system comprehensive plan was updated in 2025 and identified the King Mountain reservoir project as the primary storage addition for most of the water system service area. This study was high level and did not detail operational changes that would be needed/expected as a result of locating the storage at this site. In addition, recent and planned growth in the King Mountain area has identified needed local storage and delivery capacity increases. Lastly, the City is actively assessing two outlying urban areas for annexation which will further increase storage requirements in the system.

 

To assess the system-wide operation impacts of the proposed King Mountain Reservoir storage and confirm the required storage capacity and system upgrades, the City requires a detailed study to make recommendations. This includes confirming the planned location and layout of the King Mountain Reservoir site and confirming major pipelines/pump stations needed to support the storage and resulting changes to the impacted system operation.

SUBMITTAL
The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFQ by submitting their SOQ documents on the City website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing Office at the above address or by email Bids@cob.org.

The term of the agreement will be three (3) years, with the option to extend for one (1) additional

work slips for the work to be performed.

agreement. The basis of payment will be the actual quantities of work performed. Invoices shall

39.12. Prevailing wages shall be updated annually on the anniversary date of the IDIQ

payment & performance bond. The successful bidder is not guaranteed any minimum amount of

not result in any adjustment to contract unit prices.

The CITY OF BELLINGHAM reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses. 
Project Description
The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of preparing preliminary engineering design for Meridian Birchwood Transportation Improvements Phase 1 (Project ES564).  This will include design for both Phase I and Phase II of the planned Meridian Birchwood Transportation Improvements.  Phase I will merge the Squalicum Parkway freight truck route with Birchwood Avenue on the west side of Meridian Street intersection and decommission the Meridian/Squalicum traffic signal, including removing the unused segment of the Squalicum Parkway between Meridian Street and the new intersection of Birchwood-Squalicum.  Considerations for pedestrian, bicycles, and future trail will need to be included.  Phase II will reconstruct the Meridian/Birchwood signalized intersection into a dual-lane multimodal roundabout with a regional trail crossing the south leg of the roundabout into Cornwall Memorial Park.  This project currently has no DBE agreement goal but may be assigned for potential future work to this consultant contract if occurring during Construction phase. The major features of the project are as follows:
•	Road modification to merge two arterials and decommission/modification of existing traffic signals.
•	Roundabout design
•	Environmental documentation and preparation of permit applications, including advanced mitigation.
•	Structural design for retaining walls and culvert extensions/replacements to address fish barriers.
•	Determination of R/W needs and R/W plan preparation.
The CITY OF BELLINGHAM reserves the right to retain the services of the successful firm(s) for any subsequent phases (R/W, CN) associated with this/these project(s).

Export.Description: Notice is hereby given that The City of Bellingham (the City) is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) for the primary purpose of obtaining proposals from vendors that can provide Work Management software and implementation services. Evaluation of RFP responses and selection of Short Listed vendors will be primarily focused towards the Work Management functionality offered.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 28B-2023 from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the 12th and Finnegan Safety Improvements project (ES566) project. 

The 12th and Finnegan Safety Improvement project elements include crossing improvements at McKenzie Avenue (flashing crosswalk), Mill Avenue (full signal) and at 11th Street (flashing crosswalk), along with new sidewalk along the west side of Finnegan Way from 11th Street to Mill Avenue. Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) improvements will be included as required. The street channelization will remain unchanged but minor stormwater improvements may be required. 
Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through various City of Bellingham transportation funds and a Washington State Transportation Improvement Board grant.

The City of Bellingham solicits interest from consulting firms with expertise in Civil and Structural Engineering Design, structural construction inspection, construction engineering services, and construction management. This agreement will be for approximately two years in duration, beginning January 2024 and ending January 2026, with the option for the City of Bellingham to extend it for additional time and money if necessary.  Consultants will be considered for the following project.

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses.

Project Description
The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of construction engineering, construction management, structural inspection services, ROM management, and material documentation review for improvements to James Street/Whatcom Creek Bridge and Meador Avenue/Whatcom Creek Bridge, two federally funded projects (built as one project). The proposed improvements include James Street overcrossing of Whatcom Creek, Meador Avenue overcrossing of Whatcom Creek, roadway of James Street and Meador Avenue, sidewalks, storm sewer, and other work, all in accordance with the Contract Plans, the Contract Provisions, and the Standard Specifications. This project has 16% DBE goal. The major features of the project are as follows:

• Construction engineering, including structural engineering.
• Construction management assistance
• ROM management and material documentation review in accordance with the WSDOT LAG manual, Construction Manual and Contract PS&E package.
• Surveying checks on contractor survey.
• Inspection for structural elements in accordance with the WSDOT LAG manual, Construction Manual and Contract PS&E package.
• Materials testing and special inspections in accordance with the WSDOT LAG manual, Construction Manual and Contract PS&E package.

Consultants shall have expertise in the following:
• Traffic control measures and methodologies (in accordance with the MUTCD) to complete the project as one along with accommodation to multi-modal uses
• WSDOT Local Programs requirements for Federally Funded projects including WSDOT Local Agency Guidelines (LAG) Manual
• DBE approach and commitment
• MUTCD, NACTO, and AASHTO standards
• City of Bellingham Development Guidelines and Improvement Standards, and the Bellingham Municipal Code
• City of Bellingham and Department of Ecology standards for storm water management, per the most recently adopted version of the SWMMWW. 
• ADA Requirements
The City of Bellingham reserves the right to retain the services of the successful firm(s) for any subsequent phases (CN, CE, audit assistance, post construction support services, load rating) associated with these projects.

Evaluation Criteria 100 Points Total
Submittals will be evaluated and ranked based on the following criteria:
1. Qualification of Proposed Project Manager 15 points
2. Qualifications/Expertise of Firm  15 points
3. Ability to meet schedule 10 points
4. Approach to project 10 points
5. Familiarity with WSDOT/FHWA standards 20 points
6. Past Performance/References 15 points
7. Approach to meet the DBE goal (DBE Participation Plan) 15 points

Submittal
Submittals should include the following information: Firm name, phone, fax numbers, email; Name of Principal-in-Charge and Project Manager; and Number of employees in each firm proposed to project. Additional project information is included in the supplemental information which can be found at https://cob.procureware.com/home.  Example Submittal Information Forms to obtain consultant qualifications for Prime and Subconsultants are WSDOT form 140-565 and Form 140-566, respectively.

Please submit one paper copy and one PDF copy (on a USB drive) of your Statement of Qualifications to: City of Bellingham, 2221 Pacific Street, Bellingham, WA 98229, and Purchasing Department no later than 11:00 a.m. on December 07, 2023.  Submittals will not be accepted after that time and date.  Any questions regarding this project should be directed to City Purchasing Department, at (360) 778-7750 or email: bids@cob.org 

Estimated Procurement Schedule
Advertise RFQ  November 14 & 21, 2023
Deadline for questions  December 01, 2023
Receive SOQs December 07, 2023
Review and Rank SOQs December 21, 2023
Consultant Selection Interviews December 28, 2023
Consultant Selection/Award December 29, 2023
Scoping and Contract January 2024
Begin Work March 2024
Complete Work/End Contract January 2026

Contract Type
Contract type (method of payment) will be Negotiated Hourly Rate utilizing WSDOT’s Local Agency A&E Professional Services Negotiated Hourly Rate Consultant Agreement.  Submission of cost proposal or elements of cost shall not be submitted until a consultant selection has been made.
The Consultant(s) awarded the contract will be required to obtain and maintain a City of Bellingham Business License.

 
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Information
The City of Bellingham in accordance with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (Section 504) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), commits to nondiscrimination on the basis of disability, in all of its programs and activities. This material can be made available in an alternate format by emailing Holly Pederson, City of Bellingham ADA Coordinator at hdpederson@cob.org or by calling collect (360) 778-7950.  

Title VI Statement
The City of Bellingham, in accordance with the provisions of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (78 Stat. 252, 42 U.S.C. 2000d to 2000d-4) and the Regulations, hereby notifies all bidders that it will affirmatively ensure that in any contract entered into pursuant to this advertisement, disadvantaged business enterprises will be afforded full and fair opportunity to submit bids in response to this invitation and will not be discriminated against on the grounds of race, color, or national origin in consideration for an award.

Dates of publication in the Bellingham Herald, the Daily Journal of Commerce, and Office of Minority and Women’s Business Enterprises (OMWBE):  November 14, 2023, and November 21, 2023.

The City of Bellingham (the "City") is seeking competitive proposals from qualified firms to perform general construction work in accordance with the City's Job Order Contracting program.  A Job Order Contract is a fixed period, indefinite quantity contract that utilizes negotiated Job Orders for each individual project completed under the Job Order Contract.  Prices for each Job Order are based on the Unit Prices contained in the Construction Task Catalog® adopted by the City and the Adjustment Factors submitted by the Contractor for the entire Contract Term.  

 

The City intends to establish up to two Job Order Contracts with qualified firms through a multi-phased Request for Proposal ("RFP") process described herein and in accordance with the RCW 39.10.430-460.

 

Due to the importance of all Proposers having a clear understanding of the specifications and scope of work requirements for the City's job order contracting program, a pre-proposal meeting has been scheduled. Attendance is STRONGLY SUGGESTED so Proposers can fully comprehend the JOC procurement system and requirements of this Request for Proposal. Attendance at the pre-proposal meeting will be evidenced by the representative’s signature on the attendance roster. The City reserves the right to schedule additional pre-proposal meetings if it determines it is in the best interest of the City. 

 

The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFP by submitting their Request for Proposal (RFP) documents on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing Office at the above address or by email Bids@cob.org.

The Purchasing Office 210 Lottie Street Bellingham, WA 98225 must receive either the sealed hard copy bids/quotes/proposals no later than 11:00 AM on September 3, 2024. The sealed hard copy bids/quotes/proposals will be opened and read after the 11:00 AM deadline. The City reserves the right to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject all bids/quotes/proposals or parts of bids/quotes/proposals as may be in the best interest of the City.

Notice is hereby given that The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking submittals (RFP #35B-2019, Multiple Hearth Furnace System Inspections ) from firms interested in detailed inspection of, and report-development for, two existing multiple hearth furnaces (MHF) designed to burn City’s sludge generated as a by-product of wastewater treatment plant operations. The two MHF’s shall be inspected at separate times so that one unit always remains operational. The inspection and reporting, described in more detail throughout the RFP, shall include inspection of all essential components, refractory, castings, shell, and ancillary equipment. An inspection plan shall be submitted in advance of inspection for review by City. After inspection, a detailed report shall be developed and submitted that includes a detailed assessment of the MHFs and their component elements, estimated remaining life of components, and estimated cost of replacement or rehabilitation of MHF elements. The intent of this inspection is to provide the City with a “roadmap” to use for planning and budgeting of maintenance projects for the MHFs to keep them effectively operating for the next 15 years.

The City is requesting bids for hauling and disposal of spoils from street ditching, utility excavation, hydro excavations, and other repair activities involving excavations.

 

Ditching spoils include the materials removed in the process of cleaning road side ditches.

 

Maintenance repair spoils are materials removed in the process of repairing sanitary sewers, storm sewers, water mains and street repairs. Small quantities of asphalt or concrete may be included in this material.  Contractor shall not any increased costs for different items in the spoils on the bid form.  

 

Hydro Excavation is the use of high-pressure water to break down materials and suck them into the truck. These materials will be very wet by nature and material will be smaller than 8” in diameter

 

The City is also requesting bids for disposal only of spoils from street ditching, utility excavation, and other repair activities involving excavations.  Spoils will be hauled by the City to the contractor's designated site.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications from consulting firms with expertise in municipal utility design and rehabilitation.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 73B-2024) from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the Lower Padden Creek Water Quality project (EV185) project.

 

This project will improve water quality in Lower Padden Creek through design and future installation of a bioretention system in the median of Bill McDonald Parkway. This project will provide treatment for total suspended solids, dissolved copper, and dissolved zinc. Soil assessments at approximately 50 sites and geotechnical investigations at 10 sites in the Lower Padden Creek watershed will also be conducted to prepare an infiiltration evaluation for future projects in the Padden Creek Basin.[AF1] 

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through a Department of Ecology grant with a 15% match from the City Stormwater Fund, #430.[AF2] 

SUBMITTAL

The City requests that 1 complete copy of each proposal must be received by 11:00 a.m., Pacific time October 30, 2024.

City of Bellingham

Attn: Purchasing Office, RFQ # 73B-2024

210 Lottie Street

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this Phase 1 request for proposal (RFP) (Invitation No. 54B-2021) from service providers interested in providing future professional beneficial use services for the PPRR Biosolids Digestion project (EU-0189) project.

 

The Biosolids Beneficial Use Services project consists of transporting, processing, and beneficially using and / or marketing products derived from Class A dewatered biosolids produced by future process improvements at the City of Bellingham’s (City’s) Post Point Resource Recovery Plant (Post Point).  

This Phase 1 RFP specifically asks for information from Proposers generally regarding:

The types of further processing and technology proposed
The types of beneficial uses / products to be generated
The proposed approach to marketing products for beneficial use
The need for development of new facilities or expansion of existing facilities prior to providing services
The need for an interim or transitional service structure, as it relates to the schedule for implementing the proposed solution
The team structure that would be used to provide services (i.e. use of subcontractors)
The type of business arrangement desired with the City

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking submittals (Invitation No. 74B-2024) from engineering firms interested in providing professional design services to the Engineering Division of the Public Works Department for the Harris Avenue Multimodal Improvements (ES579).

The Harris Avenue Multimodal Improvements project will replace or upgrade water, sewer and stormwater utilities from 12th Street to 24th Street in the Fairhaven and Happy Valley neighborhoods within the City of Bellingham.  This project will include new pedestrian and bicycle facilities and resurfacing and rechannelization throughout the corridor. A bike facility study from 4th Street to 14th Street will be included to guide the proposed rechannelization.

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham utility and street funds.

Downtown Bellingham is the center of Whatcom County business and entertainment. The City of Bellingham prioritizes a safe and welcoming downtown by investing in infrastructure, marketing & economic development, cleaning, landscaping and safety services. Cleanliness, comfort and safety also attract residential, business and tourism investment. To support a downtown that is safe and friendly for people of all ages, incomes and cultures, the Contractor will provide the following unarmed foot patrols, deescalation, and customer services on behalf of the City:

 

1) Daytime patrols and outreach: Daily (8:00am-5:00pm) patrols in the public right-ofway (sidewalks, streets, alleys, etc.) and exterior of City facilities within the

 

Downtown Safety Area boundary (Figure A).

 

2) Garage patrols: Daily patrols within the City-owned Commercial Street and Railroad

 

Avenue parking facilities (Figure A), Minimum of 8 hours/day, hours to be determined

 

by the City Project Manager, in consultation with the Contractor.

 

3) Off-hour emphasis patrols: Daily evening/early morning (5:00pm-8:00am) emphasis

 

patrols within the Downtown Safety Area boundary (Figure A). Minimum of 10

 

hours/day, hours and locations(s) to be determined by the City Project Manager in

 

consultation with the Contractor and confirmed in writing prior to deployment of

 

safety personnel. Emphasis location(s) will be prioritized based on the level of

 

nuisance activity, problem behaviors, community/residential population needs and

 

requests for service.

 

The Proponent may respond to all three services requests, or individual services depending on their experience and interest. The City may contract with one or more Proponents for these services.

The Old Town Redevelopment project consists of street improvements curb to curb on Astor Street from C Street to E Street, D Street from Holly Street to Astor Street, and C Street from Holly Street to the northern terminus. The City of Bellingham Washington owns and operates the Post Point Wastewater Treatment Plant. The wastewater plant utilizes an activated sludge process and has a rated capacity of 34.3 mgd. The plant currently utilizes chlorine gas for both disinfection of treated wastewater and for odor control. We are seeking RFQs assist us in transitioning to a disinfection process that is effective, reduces regulatory mandates, and is safer for employees, residents, and visitors. The alternative process must provide rigorous and dependable disinfection and odor control. We will consider two parallel processes, however prefer one alternative that will provide a solution for both disinfection and plant odor reduction.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications from consulting firms with expertise in municipal wastewater treatment plant condition assessment, design and rehabilitation. 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 12B-2023) from consulting firms interested in providing professional consulting services for the Headworks Condition Assessment and Bypass Project (City Project Number EU195). 

The Headworks Condition Assessment and Bypass Project will include a condition assessment for various facilities within the City of Bellingham Post Point Resource Recovery Center.  This municipal owned wastewater treatment facility operates 24hrs per day and is critical City infrastructure.  The Headworks facilities, including the Screenings Facility (Bldg 110), the Headworks Building (Bldg 120), Preliminary Treatment Odor Control (Bldg 130) and Primary Clarifiers (Facility 210) were constructed in phases (1972 & 1992).  The City desires to hire a consulting firm to perform a Condition Assessment for these facilities, to better determine future planning and rehabilitation needs.  The existing facility does not include infrastructure to allow for bypass and dewatering of several sections of the influent path through these facilities.  Due to the critical nature of these facilities and the current configuration, the consultant work will also involve planning and design for temporary and/or permanent bypass to aid the assessment efforts.
A voluntary site visit and tour of the subject facilities will be held for this RFQ on February 28, 2023; interested respondents shall review the RFQ solicitation and RSVP to attend the tour.
Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham sewer utility funds.
SUBMITTAL
All proposals shall be received no later than 11:00 a.m. on March 9, 2023. Late or misdirected proposals will not be considered. Proposals shall be sent or delivered to the City of Bellingham, Purchasing Office, 2221 Pacific Street, Bellingham, WA  98229. Phone: (360) 778-7750.  The Request for Qualifications and supporting documents for bid 12B-2023 are available for download on-line at https://cob.procureware.com . 
Persons with disabilities may request this information be prepared and supplied in alternate forms by calling (360) 778-7750.

LOWER SQUALICUM CREEK ENHANCED TREATMENT - DESIGN SERVICES

 

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications from consulting firms with expertise in municipal utility design and rehabilitation.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 71B-2024 from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the Lower Squalicum Creek Enhanced Treatment (EV182) project.

The city is seeking a 90% design for stormwater BMPs for influent runoff to Lower Squalicum Creek. The initial contract will cover up to 90% design but has the potential to continue through final design and construction support as funding becomes available. This project will install bioretention or enhanced treatment BMP system(s) to treat approximately 18 acres of contributing area with more than 2,000 linear feet of roadway along Squalicum Way. Bioretention and proprietary treatment BMPs will be used to achieve enhanced treatment for all these flows that discharge to Lower Squalicum Creek, its subsequent estuary, and nearshore portions of Bellingham Bay.

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded by a Water Quality Combined Financial Assistance Agreement with the Department of Ecology.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking Statements for Qualifications (SOQs) to provide
planning, engineering, landscape architecture, archaeology, environmental evaluation,
planning, surveying, permitting assistance, construction administration, environmental
remediation, and/or cost estimating services.
The City invites all interested parties to respond to this Request of Qualifications (RFQ) by
submitting their qualifications relating to this category of work. All prospective consultants
are advised any federally funded project work will be held to federal EEO requirements.
Disadvantaged, minority and women-owned consultant firms are encouraged to respond.
The area of work includes portions of the Phase 2 development of the Waterfront
District/Cornwall Beach Area as shown in Figure 1. The area of work is contingent on the
funding available at this time. The consultant team selected for this work may be selected
to continue design into future phases of the project area as funding becomes available.
No preproposal conference is planned for this RFQ.
This project is a priority project for public access to the waterfront. This project will also
help to meet the objectives of the current Parks & Recreation Open Space Plan to provide
additional waterfront parks & trails.
This project area is located within a State cleanup site. The park development will occur
once existing cleanup activities are complete. The City of Bellingham anticipates
advancing the park grading and utilities plan for design and cost efficiencies and
incorporating the plans into the Public Works Department & Port of Bellingham cleanup
plans for the R.G. Haley and Cornwall Landfill sites.
Remediation and cleanup design for both sites are currently underway. Two separate
consultant teams are designing and permitting the R.G. Haley site for the City of
Bellingham and Cornwall Landfill site for the Port of Bellingham. The scope of this RFQ
work does not include cleanup activities, but will coordinate with current efforts to ensure
seamless transition from environmental remediation to park development. Both the
Cornwall Landfill and R.G. Haley sites are anticipated to begin cleanup construction
activities in 2021.

The City of Bellingham Public Works Department is soliciting bids for No-Lead Brass Service and Threaded Fittings

The brass alloy used for all surfaces coming in contact with potable water shall meet the requirements of UNS/CDA number C89833 as listed in ANSI/AWWAA C8002 Standard and comply with the Safe Drinking Water Act. The products produced with this alloy shall meet NSF/ANSI Standard 372 as applicable.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications from consulting firms with expertise in municipal utility design and rehabilitation.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 66B-2024 from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the Little Squalicum WQ Retrofit Phase 3 project (EV183) project.

The city is seeking a 90% design for improvements to stormwater treatment sites in the Birchwood neighborhood, located within the Little Squalicum Watershed. The initial contract will cover up to 90% design but has the potential to continue through final design and construction support as funding becomes available. This project will install bioretention or enhanced treatment BMP system(s) to treat approximately 145.50 acres of stormwater generated by the Birchwood Neighborhood. Bioretention and proprietary treatment BMPs will be used to achieve enhanced treatment for all these flows that discharge to Little Squalicum Creek, its subsequent estuary, and nearshore portions of Bellingham Bay.

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded by a Water Quality Combined Financial Assistance Agreement with the Department of Ecology.

SUBMITTAL

The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFQ by submitting their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) documents on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing Office at the above address or by email Bids@cob.org.

The Purchasing Office 210 Lottie Street Bellingham, WA 98225 must receive the electronic submittals no later than 11:00 AM on October 8, 2024. The sealed submittals will be opened and read after the 11:00 AM deadline. The City reserves the right to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject all submittals or parts of submittals as may be in the best interest of the City.

Sealed proposals for the construction of the SEHOME HILL COMMUNICATIONS TOWER -
ANTENNA INSTALLATION/TOWER DEMO EK-0001 project, will be received by the City of
Bellingham, 2221 Pacific Street, Bellingham, Washington, 98229 at the Purchasing Office until
June 11, 2020, at 11:00 a.m., and thereafter will be publicly opened and read.
The improvement consists of: the removal of antenna and equipment from the existing tower,
installation and re-installation of antenna and equipment on the new tower, demolition of the
existing tower and foundation, demolition of the existing building and foundation, landscape
restoration, one year planting establishment and irrigation and all other work in accordance with
the attached Contract Plans, these Contract Provisions and the Standard Specifications.
Price Range: $300,000 - $425,000
Plans, specifications, special provisions, basis to be used in comparing bids, proposal and
contract can be viewed at the City of Bellingham website (https://cob.procureware.com/) or seen
at the Purchasing Office, 2221 Pacific Street, Bellingham, Washington, phone (360) 778-7750.
An optional pre-bid meeting will take place on June 3, 2020 at 1 p.m. The meeting location will
be at the project site and shall follow appropriate safety guidelines outlined in Section 1-07.1.
All proposals must be upon the Bid Proposal form provided by the City of Bellingham and must
be accompanied by a certified check, cashier's check, cash, money order or bid bond payable to
the Finance Director in an amount equal to or exceeding five percent (5%) of the total bid. No
other form of bid security is acceptable.
The right is reserved to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject any
and all bids, or to waive irregularities not affecting substantial rights.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking submittals (Invitation No. 83B-2023) from engineering firms interested in providing professional design services to the Engineering Division of the Public Works Department for the Little Squalicum Creek Water Quality Retrofits – Phase 2 – Design (EV-0177).

The Little Squalicum Creek Water Quality Retrofits – Phase 1 project will improve water quality in Little Squalicum Creek through the installation of bioretention and other enhanced treatment BMPs to treat stormwater generated by 115 acres of residential development in the Birchwood neighborhood within the City of Bellingham.  This project will provide stormwater treatment for total suspended solids (TSS), oil (total petroleum hydrocarbons), dissolved copper, dissolved zinc, and total phosphorus and will also reduce flows to Little Squalicum Creek by increasing stormwater infiltration.

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham funds and a Washington State Department of Ecology Grant.

The City of Bellingham is interested in contracting with a consultant to complete annual  monitoring of the Post Point Heron Colony for up to five years beginning in February 2022. Work may include all or some of the monitoring years listed above. There is no guarantee as to the amount or extent of work under this contract.

The Post Point Heron Colony is the only known heron nesting site in the City of Bellingham. The colony was first documented in 2000, at its present location in south Bellingham’s Fairhaven district, adjacent to the Post Point Resource Recovery Plant. The colony is located in a forest patch on City owned property, situated between the wastewater plant and privately owned undeveloped land. Due to the sensitivity of the heronry and its uniqueness within the city, Bellingham Public Works requested a management plan (2003), followed by a scientific baseline study of the colony in 2005 to document breeding chronology, nesting activities, colony status and habitat use. Following these efforts, annual monitoring of the colony began in 2005 as a conservation measure due to the colony’s local significance and unique critical habitat. Updated Post Point Heron Colony Management Guidelines were developed in 2019. Annual monitoring has continued through 2021 consistent with these 2019 guidelines. The City is interested in continuing monitoring beyond 2021. Information on the Post Point Heron Colony, including past monitoring reports and the Point Heron Colony Management

The improvement consists of rebuilding the existing Park Place Water Quality Facility with an improved phosphorus removal media and facility reconfiguration. The purpose of the Water System Plan is to identify system deficiencies that may exist with the following - storage, demand, treatment, pressure zones, fire flow, and the Lake Whatcom Intake.  The Plan should provide guidance over the next 20 years on how best to manage capital improvements, development, and maintenance requirements associated with the water system.  Additionally, the City is seeking calibration and staff education of the City’s InfoWater computer model, along with a rate study.  

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham water utility fund.

The improvement consists of: The project includes construction of a new arterial street from James Street, under I-5, to the Squalicum Parkway/Birchwood Avenue intersection.  This work will include retaining walls, earthwork, concrete curb and gutter and sidewalk, street lighting, installation of a watermain, installation of a stormwater collection system, stormwater treatment vaults, stormwater pond, traffic light at James Street, paving and striping of pavement.

The City of Bellingham solicits interest from consulting firms with expertise in Civil, Structural Engineering and Railway Crossing Design. This agreement will be for approximately two years in duration, beginning September 2024 and ending December 2026, with the option for the City of Bellingham to extend it for additional time and money if necessary.  Consultants will be considered for the following project.

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses.

Project Description

The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of preparing preliminary engineering design for the Pine Street Crossing project. The proposed improvements include installation of surface improvements to support a quiet zone compliant crossing installation by Burlington North Sante Fe (BNSF). Pedestrian and bicycle improvements will be included within the new crossing and along Wharf Street and Pine Street to connect to other regional facilities. Minor utility upgrades and updated illumination will also be included in the project scope. The major features of the project are as follows:

 

Roadway improvements to support pedestrian, bicycle and automobile facilities through a quiet zone compatible crossing over two existing Burlington Northern Santa Fe (BNSF) railway lines (mainline and maintenance leg).
Structural design for retaining walls and spans to support new pedestrian and bicycle facilities along Wharf Street.
Surface feature design for all modes along Pine Street and connections to the Salish Landing Park, Bellingham Shipping Terminal access and Cornwall Avenue
Municipal utility connections and upgrades needed to support the project.
Determination of Right-of-Way (ROW) needs and ROW plan preparation

 

Consultants shall have expertise in the following:

Federal Railway Administration (FRA) design standards for quiet zone crossings.
BNSF crossing requirements and construction regulations
Traffic control measures and methodologies (in accordance with the Manual of Uniform Traffic Control (MUTCD)) to complete the project as one along with accommodation to multi-modal uses
WSDOT Local Programs and Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) requirements for Federally Funded projects including WSDOT Local Agency Guidelines (LAG) Manual
DBE approach and commitment
Environmental documentation and preparation of permit applications, including NEPA and shoreline use regulations
MUTCD, NACTO, and AASHTO standards
City of Bellingham Development Guidelines and Improvement Standards, and the Bellingham Municipal Code
City of Bellingham and Department of Ecology standards for storm water management, per the most recently adopted version of the SWMMWW.
ADA Requirements

 

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to retain the services of the successful firm(s) for any subsequent phases (ROW, CN) associated with these projects.

 

All prospective consultants are advised that federally funded projects will be held to Federal Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) requirements.

 

Submittal

All submittals shall include a signed cover letter including the following information: Firm name, phone, fax numbers, email; Name of Principal-in-Charge and Project Manager; and Number of employees in each firm proposed to project. Additional project information is included in the supplemental information which can be found at https://cob.procureware.com/home. Submittal Information Forms for each Prime and Subconsultant listed in submittal should be included on WSDOT Form 140-565 and Form 140-566, respectively.

 

Submittals shall be limited to a maximum of sixteen 8-1/2" by 11" pages (sixteen single-sided or eight pages double-sided), not including the title page (limited to one page), table of contents (limited to one page), resumes (limited to one page for each individual) and forms 140-565 and 140-566 (limited to one per company). Submittals over the maximum page size limit will not be considered.

 

Please submit one paper copy of your Statement of Qualifications to: City of Bellingham, 210 Lottie Street, Bellingham, WA 98225, and Purchasing Department no later than 11:00 a.m. on June 26, 2024.  Submittals will not be accepted after that time and date.  Any questions regarding this project should be directed to City Purchasing Department, at (360) 778-7750 or email: bids@cob.org 

 

Contract type (method of payment) will be Negotiated Hourly Rate utilizing WSDOT’s Local Agency A&E Professional Services Negotiated Hourly Rate Consultant Agreement.  Submission of cost proposal or elements of cost shall not be submitted until a consultant selection has been made. The Consultant(s) awarded the contract will be required to obtain and maintain a City of Bellingham Business License.


 

Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Information

The City of Bellingham in accordance with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (Section 504) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), commits to nondiscrimination on the basis of disability, in all of its programs and activities. This material can be made available in an alternate format by emailing Holly Pederson, City of Bellingham ADA Coordinator at hdpederson@cob.org or by calling collect (360) 778-7950. 

Title VI Statement

The City of Bellingham, in accordance with the provisions of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (78 Stat. 252, 42 U.S.C. 2000d to 2000d-4) and the Regulations, hereby notifies all bidders that it will affirmatively ensure that in any contract entered into pursuant to this advertisement, disadvantaged business enterprises will be afforded full and fair opportunity to submit bids in response to this invitation and will not be discriminated against on the grounds of race, color, or national origin in consideration for an award.

 

Dates of publication in the Bellingham Herald, the Daily Journal of Commerce, and Office of Minority and Women’s Business Enterprises (OMWBE):  June 4, 2024, and June 11, 2024.

Scope of works include planned maintenance as well as emergency and nonemergency repair work.  All work will be performed on a time and materials basis using the hourly rate(s) and parts and materials markup percentage contained in the contractor’s Bid Proposal, which will be attached to and made a part of the IDIQ agreement.  The term of the agreement will be three (3) years, with the option to extend for one (1) additional year.  Over the term of the agreement, the City will identify specific work assignments and request a written quotation from the contractor for the work.

The City has identified the following required tasks, at a minimum, necessary to
complete the preparation of a 10-year Facilities Master Plan:
• Stakeholder/Community Involvement - Develop and implement a community
involvement process to engage a broad range of stakeholders in assessing current
facilities and future community needs.
• Library Facility Assessment - Complete an assessment of all Library facilities,
including dedicated public library space at three college locations. Review space
utilization, configuration, physical arrangement, and suitability for Library services.
Make recommendations for optimal space utilization, location and adjacencies of
functional public and non-public areas.
• Trend Analysis - Consider and evaluate national trends and best practices as they
relate to Bellingham Public Library and City of Bellingham planning needs and
incorporate this broader lens in final Facilities Master Plan report.
• Future Footprint Assessment - Assess and make recommendations as to the
appropriate size and location of the Central Library and branches within current
service area, accounting for forecasted population growth and City of Bellingham
urban growth areas. Identify whether additional facilities are needed, recommended
size & type of facilities and in what areas they should be located. Identify potential
locations for additional stand-alone community Drop Boxes.
• Facility Recommendations - Provide recommendations for prioritizing into actionable
steps any renovations to the current facilities which are suggested over the 10-year
span of the Facilities Master Plan.
• 1st Plan Draft - Preparation of written draft Facilities Master Plan and communication
method with Library for review and direction.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) solicits interest from consulting firms with expertise in Civil and Structural Engineering design, fish biology and habitat requirements, cultural resources, and stream hydrology and hydraulics. This agreement will be for approximately one year in duration, beginning January 2025 and ending January 2026, with the option for the City of Bellingham to extend it for additional time and money if necessary.  Consultants will be considered for the following project.


The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses.

 

Project Description

The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of preparing conceptual plans and 30% engineering design plans for up to three (3) fish passage barrier improvements as identified by City of Bellingham, Nooksack Indian Tribe, Lummi Nation, and Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW) as part of their work on the voluntary 2022 Fish Barrier Culvert Remediation Project MOA (www.cob.org/culverts). The exact location of these projects is to be determined, but they will be on Squalicum, Whatcom and/or Padden Creeks in the City of Bellingham, Washington. Exact barriers will be determined by the City prior to contracting.

The City will also require survey for base maps, topography and existing utilities, geotechnical evaluation, hydrologic and hydraulic analysis, and fish passage evaluation. Other future services may include riparian landscape design, cultural resources survey, habitat analysis, environmental permitting, right-of-way support, final design, construction management, public outreach, etc.   The City will be the lead for the right-of-way acquisition, if needed, as well as the public outreach efforts for this project. [FAK1] [JB2] This project will continue to bid-ready plans, specifications, permitting, and estimate of costs for some or all the barriers as funding becomes available. The City of Bellingham reserves the right to retain the services of the successful firm(s) for any subsequent phases (Final Design, audit assistance, construction and post-construction support services) associated with these projects.

NOAA’s Restoring Fish Passage through Barrier Removal granted $300,000 to the Nooksack Indian Tribe and will contribute to the overall costs for this stage of the project. This project is likely to receive federal funding and subject to federal requirements[FAK3] [JB4]  outlined in the Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT), and Brian Abbott Fish Barrier Removal Board (FBRB) design standards.


The major features of the project are as follows:

Feasibility and Alternatives Analysis Report.
Generate electronic base map and digital terrain model from field survey information using AutoCAD Civil 3D in accordance with City of Bellingham CAD Standards - https://www.cob.org/gov/rules/standards/Pages/CAD-Standards.aspx
Surveying of project area as needed for design by a registered land surveyor licensed in the State of Washington. The survey must be completed using NAVD88 datum.
Cultural resources survey.
Prepare Conceptual Plan
Design Reports
Prepare 30% design plans, specifications, and cost estimates.
Hydrologic and hydraulic analysis.
Geotechnical analysis.
FUTURE: Assist the City in applying for and obtaining federal, State, local, and environmental permits.
FUTURE: Provide public outreach support.
FUTURE: Cultural resources surveying.
FUTURE: Prepare final design plans, specifications, and cost estimates.

Due to the complexity of this project, work may include all, some or none, of the items listed above. There is no guarantee as to the amount or extent of work under this contract. 

 

Consultants shall have expertise in the following:

NOAA Fisheries Restoring Tribal Priority Fish Passage through Barrier Removal Grant
US Department of Commerce Financial Assistance requirements
Brian Abbott FBRB Manual 22 and grant requirements
Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT) and Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) standards
WSDOT Local Agency Guidelines (LAG) Manual
Washington’s Stream Habitat Restoration Guidelines (2012)
WDFW Water Crossing Design Guidelines
City of Bellingham Development Guidelines and Improvement Standards, and the Bellingham Municipal Code
City of Bellingham and Department of Ecology standards for storm water management, per the most recently adopted version of the SWMMWW.
Fish biology and habitat requirements
Landscape design of riparian and aquatic resources
Stream hydrology and hydraulics
Design of structures within public Rights-of-Way
Structural design for culverts and bridges
Geotechnical analysis
Cultural resource compliance
Traffic control measures and methodologies that accommodate multi-modal uses
Permitting of similar projects at the local, state, and federal levels
Public outreach and engagement

 

Evaluation Criteria                                                                100 Points Total

Submittals will be evaluated and ranked based on the following criteria:

Qualification of Key Personnel                                          15 points
Qualifications/Expertise of Team                                      15 points
Ability to meet schedule                                                    10 points
Approach to project                                                          15 points
Familiarity with WSDOT/FHWA/FBRB standards              15 points
Past Performance/References                                          15 points
Approach to meet the DBE/SBE goal (Participation Plan) 15 points

 

Submittal

Submittals shall include a signed cover letter including the following information: Firm name, phone, fax numbers, email; Name of Principal-in-Charge and Project Manager; and Number of employees in each firm proposed to project. Additional project information is included in the supplemental information which can be found at https://cob.procureware.com/home.  Submittal Information Forms for each Prime and Subconsultant listed in submittal should be included on WSDOT Form 140-565 and Form 140-566, respectively.

Submittals shall be limited to a maximum of sixteen 8-1/2" by 11" pages (sixteen single-sided or eight pages double-sided), not including the title page (limited to one page), table of contents (limited to one page), resumes (limited to one page for each individual) and forms 140-565 and 140-566 (limited to one per company). Submittals over the maximum page size limit will not be considered.


The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFQ by submitting their Request for Qualification (RFQ) documents on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing Office at the above address or by email Bids@cob.org. 

The Purchasing Office 210 Lottie Street Bellingham, WA 98225 must receive the electronic bids/quotes/proposals no later than 11:00 AM on September 24th, 2024. The sealed electronic bids/quotes/proposals will be opened and read after the 11:00 AM deadline. The City reserves the right to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject all bids/quotes/proposals or parts of bids/quotes/proposals as may be in the best interest of the City.
