The City of Bellingham solicits interest from consulting firms with expertise in Civil and Structural Engineering Design. This agreement will be for approximately two years in duration, beginning August 2024 and ending September 2026, with the option for the City of Bellingham to extend it for additional time and money if necessary.  Consultants will be considered for the following project.

 

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses.

 

Project Description

The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of preparing preliminary engineering design for the Eldridge Squalicum Creek Bridge Replacement project. The proposed improvements include replacing the existing six span reinforced concrete t-beam structure with a three span prestressed concrete girder structure. Pedestrian and bicycle improvements will be included on the new bridge. Utilities on the existing bridge will need to be maintained in service during and after construction. This project has a 17% DBE goal. The major features of the project are as follows:

 

Roadway, bicycle and pedestrian improvements on new bridge and approaches
Structural design for the new bridge structure
Utility design for new bridge and temporary utility bypass during construction
Environmental documentation and preparation of permit applications, including NEPA
Determination of R/W needs and R/W plan preparation

 

 

Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Information

The City of Bellingham in accordance with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (Section 504) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), commits to nondiscrimination on the basis of disability, in all of its programs and activities. This material can be made available in an alternate format by emailing Holly Pederson, City of Bellingham ADA Coordinator at hdpederson@cob.org or by calling collect (360) 778-7950.

This expansion of the current Operations Center will involve replacement of the existing WTA building and Wash Rack Building. The current WTA building is located at 2221 Nevada Street. The City is looking to replace the existing WTA building with a new vehicle and equipment storage building that will include heated vehicle and equipment storage and workshop spaces. The new single-story building will include restroom facilities, Operations wood shop, vehicle storage space for: 6 Vactor trucks, 3 street sweepers, snow and ice equipment, tractors, mowers, operations vehicles and equipment, and incorporation of a new wash rack into the building. The scope of work will include programming, pre-design and feasibility, planning, design, construction documentation for bidding. The consultant tasks shall take place within a schedule anticipating completion of building design and permitting by November 2020. Work may involve expansion of the existing playground envelope to accommodate new equipment and fall zones. The City has not determined which areas to expand into. Bloedel Donovan Park is located at 2214 Electric Avenue, Bellingham WA 98225.

 

Rock Hill Park shall involve the replacement of existing playground equipment and potential expansion of playground opportunities. Work may also include site planning to enhance universal accessibility, walkway connections to a parking area broadening the range of recreational opportunities to under used areas in the park, notwithstanding potential limitations of use in WSDOT managed ROW. These playground projects shall comprise one package and indivisible. SOQ shall include both playground projects. 

 

The work to be performed by the CONSULTANT consists of any and all services and materials necessary to accomplish the work including, but not limited to, the following: work within an identified budget, conduct reconnaissance and data collection, continuous management of the project, maintain close contact with the city project manager(s), attend periodic meetings with members of project boards, committees or stakeholders, prepare SEPA application, EIS, BE, CAO report or any other required environmental documentation, verify and analyze the existing site survey and facilities, data gap analysis and recommendation, provide 30%, 60%, 90% and 100% bid-ready construction plans and drawings, provide preliminary and final cost estimates, submit concept phase plans, elevations, renderings and sections to staff for review & comment, provide concept drawings to neighborhood groups, and park board for review, attend meetings and give formal presentations as needed, prepare as-built.

 

Due to the complexity of this project, work may include all, some or none of the items listed above. There is no guarantee as to the amount or extent of work under this contract.

 

SUBMITTAL: Qualification submittals are to be prepared in such a way as to provide a straight forward, concise delineation of the proposer’s capabilities to satisfy the requirements of this RFQ.

 

Submittals shall be limited to 12 pages (6 double-sided pages). Resumes will not be counted towards the page limit.

 

Emphasis will be concentrated on conformance to the RFQ instructions, responsiveness to the RFQ requirements, overall completeness and clarity of content.

 

Submittals will be evaluated and ranked based on the following criteria: 1) Qualifications & Experience; 2) Organization; 3) Technical Knowledge, 4) Projects; 5) Schedule; 6) References.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 4B-2024) from consulting firms interested in providing professional engineering services for the Incinerator Emissions Control Upgrades Study project, City Project Number EU199. 

The Post Point Resource Recovery Plant operates two Multi-Hearth Incinerator units and supporting Emission Control systems. These Sewage Sludge Incinerators reduce sewage sludge to inert ash for final solids disposal.  This municipal owned wastewater treatment facility operates 24hrs per day and is critical City infrastructure.  The Incinerator Emissions Control Upgrades Study project will review the current Sewage Sludge Incinerator air emission control systems and determine the feasibility of additional improvements and upgrades to comply with more stringent air emission control requirements and reduce air emissions.  Additional tasks include consulting services to the City in support of the development of an Air Operating Permit by the regional air authority (Northwest Clean Air Agency), and services related to rehabilitation of the Continuous Emission Monitoring System and Wet ElectroStatic Precipitator components.

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham sewer utility funds.
SUBMITTAL
All proposals shall be received no later than 11:00 a.m. on February 22, 2024. Late or misdirected proposals will not be considered. Proposals shall be sent or delivered to the City of Bellingham, Purchasing Office, 210 Lottie St., Bellingham, WA  98225. Phone: (360) 778-7750.  The Request for Qualifications and supporting documents for bid 4B-2024 are available for download on-line at https://cob.procureware.com .

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 7B-2024 from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the Lake Whatcom Vault Retrofits, Phase 1 (city project # EV176) project.

This planned project is part of the effort aimed at reducing phosphorus loading in stormwater through retrofitting existing stormwater treatment facilities to maximize nutrient-removal.  Up to five existing, city-owned, public stormwater facilities will be retrofitted with treatment systems designed for phosphorus removal along with TSS and dissolved copper and zinc.  The preferred option is POST media (GULD from the Department of Ecology Assessment Protocol – Ecology (TAPE) Program) as it is expected to provide the highest phosphorus removal rate for the lowest lifetime maintenance cost.    

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through City of Bellingham stormwater funds and a Stormwater Financial Assistance Program (SFAP) grant from Department of Ecology.

The City of Bellingham is soliciting competitive bids for the purpose of establishing a public works contract for on-call electrical services.  Work will include planned maintenance as well as emergency and nonemergency repair work.  All work will be performed on a time and materials basis using the hourly rate(s) and parts and materials markup percentage contained in the contractor’s Bid Proposal, which will be attached to and made a part of the on-call agreement.  The term of the on-call agreement will be three (3) years, with the option to extend for one (1) additional year.  Over the term of the agreement, the City will identify specific work assignments and request a written quotation from the contractor for the work.  The contractor will provide an itemized written quotation for each work assignment using the hourly rate(s) contained in its Bid Proposal.  The City will review the Contractor’s quotation and, upon approval, issue a purchase order for the work.  Each purchase order will be issued under the on-call agreement and will be subject to its general terms and conditions.

General Contractor/Construction Management (GC/CM) companies (Respondents) are invited to submit Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) for the preconstruction services and potential construction services for the Post Point Resource Recovery Plant Project (Project) EU189 in accordance with the Heavy Civil Construction process of the Revised Code of Washington (RCW) 39.10.

 Project Scope: The Project involves the replacement of the City of Bellingham’s (Owner’s) Post Point Resource Recovery incineration process. The incinerators will be replaced with an anaerobic digestion system to produce Class A biosolids product. The anaerobic digestion process will also produce biogas, which is planned for injection in the local natural gas pipeline as a renewable fuel. The Project also includes ancillary upgrades to the solids thickening and dewatering processes, solids screening, digester biogas treatment, and electrical and instrumentation system, and includes a “side stream” treatment process to remove nitrogen. A new Resource Recovery Center is included to replace aging and inadequate facilities, including operations center, environmental education, laboratory, and maintenance facilities.

 Pursuant to RCW 39.10, Alternative Public Works Contracting Procedures, the Owner intends to award a contract for GC/CM services utilizing a two-step competitive process to select the most qualified contractor.

The Post Point Resource Recovery Plant at 200 McKenzie Avenue, is a Publicly Owned Treatment Works facility that treats an average of 12 million gallons per day of municipal wastewater for the City of Bellingham. The facility operates 24 hours per day, 7 days a week, and is critical infrastructure to the City of Bellingham. The Post Point Resource Recovery Plant discharges treated effluent through an outfall located in Bellingham Bay, a part of the Puget Sound and Salish Sea.

The Washington State Department of Ecology issued the Puget Sound Nutrient General Permit (PSNGP #WAG994535) effective January 1, 2022. This General Permit is expected to be the initial phase of a multi-year (and multiple-permit) effort to limit the discharge of Total Inorganic Nitrogen (TIN) from Municipal Wastewater Treatment Plants. The Post Point Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) is identified as a Dominant Loader WWTP under the permit. The PSNGP stipulates several requirements for Dominant Loaders to comply with the current permit, including development of a Nitrogen Optimization Plan & Report, Nutrient Reduction Evaluation (NRE), Source Control, Corrective Actions (if TIN exceedance occurs), and other requirements. The Nutrient Reduction Evaluation additionally requires an analysis of all known, available and reasonable treatment (AKART) approaches for TIN reduction, site specific analysis of alternate effluent management options, economic evaluation, and an Environmental Justice (EJ) review. The NRE is expected guide capital planning efforts toward compliance with future, more stringent effluent limits via implementation of additional treatment works.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking Statements of Qualifications (SOQ) (Invitation
No. 51B-2020) from consultants interested in providing professional design services to
the City of Bellingham for the Orchard Drive Extension (Birchwood Ave) project (ES-
0440). Disadvantaged, minority and women-owned consultant firms are encouraged to
respond. Upon consideration of the submittals, the City will negotiate final terms with
the selected party.
Interested consultants should deliver four (4) copies of their SOQ to the Purchasing
Office, 2221 Pacific St., Bellingham, WA 98229, no later than 11:00 a.m., PST,
Wednesday September 16, 2020. Submittals and their envelopes should be clearly
marked with the name and address of the Proponent and should be marked “Orchard
Drive Extension (Birchwood Ave), Bid No. 51B-2020". DO NOT ADDRESS YOUR
ENVELOPE TO AN INDIVIDUAL.
RFQ documents can be viewed at the City of Bellingham website
(https://cob.procureware.com/) or seen at the Purchasing Office, 2221 Pacific Street,
Bellingham, Washington, phone (360) 778-7750. Questions about the RFQ should be
submitted on the City's bidding website.
Background Information
The project includes construction of a new arterial street from the James Street/Orchard
Drive intersection, westward under I-5 in an existing grade separated crossing, to the
Birchwood Ave/Squalicum Parkway intersection. Included with the project are retaining
walls, earth moving, watermain, sanitary sewer, stormwater collection and treatment
systems, a stormwater pond, curb and gutter, sidewalk, wetland mitigation sites, asphalt
paving, street lights, traffic lights and pavement striping.
The project will provide an arterial connection between the northern portion of the city with
the city core, as well as a more direct core to the regional hospital. The site is currently
on a former railroad grade, flood control berm, and through forested wetlands. The new
street will be a multimodal connection including bicycle lanes and sidewalks.
The project is funded by Federal STP Funds and Connection Washington Funds

The City of Bellingham is soliciting statements of qualification from interested consultants to provide services for the redesign of Fountain Plaza, located at the corner of Meridian and Broadway Streets.

The City invites all interested parties to submit their qualifications for architectural, engineering, landscape architectural, surveying, permitting, environmental, cost estimating and/or all related services for this project. The City is specifically looking for a consultant team with experience in Public Library design who will involve the public and city staff during the design process, with a focus on equity and inclusion.  Disadvantaged, minority and women-owned consultant firms are encouraged to respond.  The Consultant performing the work is expected to provide services including, but not limited to: development of concept design to final construction documents (plans, specifications, cost estimates, and permitting), stormwater site plan to satisfy state and local regulations, and geotechnical expertise relating to erosion, seismic, and all hazard areas, as well as all other project requirements.

 

The renovation of the existing Bellingham Public Library at 210 Central Avenue includes, but is not limited to:  HVAC electrification, renovation of the ground floor, renovation of the main floor entrance, redesign of the existing help desk on the main floor to improve security and staff safety, renovation of the upper floor, and upgrades to the exterior / esthetic qualities of the building and landscaping. 

 

Submittals of Qualifications are due no later than January 24, 2023 at 11 A.M. in the City of Bellingham Purchasing Office, located at 2221 Pacific Street Bellingham WA 98226. Contact City Purchasing Office at 360-778-7750, or bids@cob.org

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written proposals from consulting firms with expertise in environmental planning.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking submittals (Invitation No. 64B-2023) from consulting firms interested in providing professional planning services to the City of Bellingham to update the Shoreline Master Program (SMP) Restoration Plan. This effort is in support of the City’s overall SMP update, more commonly referred to as a “periodic review.”

A SMP is the local land-use policies and regulations that regulates development along the City’s shorelines or, “shorelines of the state.” The City of Bellingham is one of more than 260 Washington cities and counties that have SMPs. The City’s shorelines of the state are Bellingham Bay, Lake Whatcom and Lake Padden, Chuckanut, Whatcom and Squalicum Creeks and Padden Creek upstream to McKenzie Avenue.
Local jurisdictions are required by the state to complete a periodic review, or update, to their SMP. The City’s SMP was last updated in 2013 and is codified in Title 22 of our Municipal Code (BMC Title 22, Shorelines). The City of Bellingham is currently updating their SMP. The majority of the update will be completed by City staff; however, the City is seeking consultant support for the Restoration Plan component. The purpose of an SMP Restoration Plan is to include goals, policies, and actions for restoration of impaired shoreline ecological functions over time (WAC 173-26-201(2)(f)).
SUBMITTAL

All proposals shall be received no later than 11:00 a.m. on Thursday August 17, 2023. Late or misdirected proposals will not be considered. Proposals shall be sent or delivered to the City of Bellingham, Purchasing Office, 2221 Pacific Street, Bellingham, WA  98229. Sealed proposals for PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT FOR IDIQ ASPHALT PAVEMENT REPAIR SERVICES will be received by the City of Bellingham through its Purchasing Office at 210 Lottie Street, Bellingham, WA 98225 until January 25, 2024, at 11:00 a.m., and thereafter will be publicly opened and read.

 

The City of Bellingham is soliciting competitive bids for the purpose of establishing a public works contract for using defined (fixed) unit priced asphalt pavement repair services.  The work consists of: Various asphalt pavement repairs throughout the City of Bellingham and its greater water and sewer service areas. Bid award is based on estimated work which is provided in the bid specifications for bid comparison purposes only. Actual work will be as needed.

 

The term of the agreement will be three (3) years, with the option to extend for one (1) additional year.  Over the term of the agreement, the City will identify specific work assignments and issue work slips for the work to be performed.

 

All work will be performed according to the unit prices contained in the contractor’s Bid Proposal (subject to annual CPI adjustment), which will be attached to and made a part of the IDIQ agreement.  The basis of payment will be the actual quantities of work performed. Invoices shall be submitted once work is completed.  The City will inspect work and pay invoice within 30 days (Net 30).

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking written statements of qualifications from consulting firms with expertise in municipal utility design and rehabilitation.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 2B-2025) from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the Lincoln Creek Restoration: Fraser Street to Whatcom Creek project (EV181) project.

 

The Lincoln Creek Restoration: Fraser Street to Whatcom Creek project requires the removal of a 64” corrugated metal pipe and replacement with an open channel for Lincoln Creek through the Haskell Business Park. The project intends to find the best balance of open channel and habitat creation, while maintaining as much existing improvements in the Haskell Business Park as is reasonable. Services, including professional engineering services, permitting support, environmental services, and surveying may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through the City of Bellingham Storm Fund.

SUBMITTAL

The City invites all interested parties to respond to this RFQ by submitting their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) documents on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing Office at the above address or by email Bids@cob.org. The Purchasing Office, 210 Lottie Street Bellingham, WA 98225 must receive the electronic submittals no later than 11:00 AM on January 15, 2025. The sealed electronic submittals will be opened and read after the 11:00 AM deadline.

Persons with disabilities may request this information be prepared and supplied in alternate forms by calling (360) 778-7750.

The City of Bellingham, in accordance with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 78 Stat. 252, 42 U.S.C. 2000d to 2000d-4 and Title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, Department of Transportation, subtitle A, Office of the Secretary, Part 21, nondiscrimination in federally assisted programs of the Department of Transportation issued pursuant to such Act, hereby notifies all bidders that it will affirmatively ensure that in any contract entered into pursuant to this advertisement, disadvantaged business enterprises as defined at 49 CFR Part 26 will be afforded full and fair opportunity to submit bids in response to this invitation and will not be discriminated against on the grounds of race, color, national origin or sex in consideration for an award.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is issuing this request for qualifications (RFQ) (Invitation No. 69B-2023) from consulting firms interested in providing professional design services for the James Street Multimodal – Segments 3 and 4 (ES565) project.

 James Street is the only north-south transportation corridor serving the King Mountain Neighborhood. WTA high-frequency Gold GO Line Route 331 service exists, but traditional sidewalks and bike lanes are not financially feasible. A 12-foot-wide multiuse pathway was identified as the preferred alternative. Segments 3 and 4 would create a continuous multiuse pathway between Telegraph Road and Gooding Avenue and would link to the Telegraph Road Multimodal Improvements, James/Bakerview roundabout and King Mtn Safe Route to School sidewalks and bike lanes. Considerations for fish passage in culverts, fiber infrastructure and future utility services through the corridor may also be included in the project scope. 

Services, including professional engineering services, and construction engineering and/or administration, may be added/removed from the contract contingent upon funding availability and project needs. This project is funded through various City of Bellingham Street and Transportation funds.

The vendor must be able to provide various sedan, pickup truck, and
heavy-duty vehicle interior and exterior detailing services per requested,
see attached Exhibit A. The vendor must provide pickup and delivery
service to the City of Bellingham, Fleet Maintenance Facility, 2221 Pacific
Street, Bellingham, WA 98229 by a licensed and insured driver. If the
equipment requires a CDL license, the vehicle will be delivered and
picked up by the City. The City will provide a work order and a scope of
services to be performed with each vehicle. An invoice should be issued
upon delivery of the vehicle to the City.

The City of Bellingham is creating a Home Electrification Pilot Program (HEPP) to pursue community carbon pollution reduction goals and to help understand barriers associated with installing electric appliances in low and moderate income homes in Bellingham. This pilot program will aim to install electric appliances in the homes of low and moderate income residents and prepare the City and the Consultant to expand this program to a wider portion of the community by exploring several dimensions of home electrification, including:  

 

Perceptions of homeowners regarding electric appliances
Communications to homeowners about home electrification options and processes, including how to best reach homeowners about opportunities.
Which aspects of home electrification are homeowners most interested in
Primary challenges that installers will face in integrating electric appliances into homes
Real-world costs associated with home electrification
Impacts on resident energy bills and equipment maintenance costs
The level of effort involved in electrifying homes, including home assessments, client education, contracting and project management
Strengths and challenges of the City and Consultant relative to the pursuit of residential electrification
Homeowner satisfaction regarding electric appliances after installation and use and how to improve the overall program process for homeowners

Sealed proposals for the construction of the JULIANNA PARK IMPROVEMENTS PD2028-7C project, will be received by the City of Bellingham, 2221 Pacific Street, Bellingham, Washington, 98229 at the Purchasing Office until March 31, 2020, at 11:00 a.m., and thereafter will be publicly opened and read.

 

The improvement consists of erosion control, clearing, grubbing, vehicular bridge, culverts, drainage structures, electrical, utilities, concrete, limestone trail, mulching, seeding, and all other work as necessary to complete the project.

This Contract improves pedestrian and bicycle safety and efficiency within public right-of-way at the Northwest Avenue/West Bakerview Road intersection.  Work consists of installing temporary erosion control measures; roadway excavation; grading with gravel and crushed surfacing; removal of certain existing site features; minor drainage modifications; upgrading pedestrian access routes and safety elements; installing concrete curbs, gutters, sidewalks, traffic islands, ADA ramps, and landings; modifying traffic and pedestrian signal components; removing existing and adding new improved-visibility pavement markings; paving with HMA; roadway surveying; traffic control; trimming and cleanup; record drawings; and other work, all in accordance with the attached Contract Plans, these Contract Provisions, and the Standard Specifications.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to provide engineering, surveying, environmental, and other services for planning, studying, and assessing development implications and options of the City’s next neighborhood park. This project will involve multiple areas of expertise not limited to those mentioned above.

 

In 2020 the City purchased approximately 27.5 acres of undeveloped land located on E. Bakerview Rd., between Deemer Road and James Street, as shown on attachment ‘C’ of this RFQ. The City was awarded grant funding from the Washington State Recreation and Conservation Office (RCO) to fund a portion of the acquisition of this property. Development and use of the site must comply with the terms of the Grant Agreement (Agreement) between the City and RCO.

 

The property will function as a neighborhood park and provide a significant multimodal trail hub connecting existing and future trails. The western third of the property contains a mix of cleared, level ground suitable for active and passive recreation facilities that may include playground, restrooms, sport courts, and trails. The eastern two-thirds of the parcel is heavily forested and contains wetlands and two mapped creeks, Cammack and North Fork Baker, as well as a culverted creek, Landon. The City wishes for a portion of the site to be developed as affordable housing.

The City of Bellingham is soliciting competitive bids for the purpose of establishing a public works contract for on-call HVAC repair services. Work will include emergency and nonemergency repair work. All work will be performed on a time and materials basis using the hourly rate(s) and parts and materials markup percentage contained in the contractor’s Bid Proposal, which will be attached to and made a part of the on-call agreement. The term of the on-call agreement will be three (3) years, with the option to extend for one (1) additional year. Over the term of the agreement, the City will identify specific work assignments and request a written quotation from the contractor for the work. The contractor will provide an itemized written quotation for each work assignment using the hourly rate(s) contained in its Bid Proposal. The City will review the Contractor’s quotation and, upon approval, issue a purchase order for the work. Each purchase order will be issued under the on-call agreement and will be subject to its general terms and conditions.

The contractor shall pay prevailing wages for all work that is subject to the requirements of RCW 39.12. Prevailing wages shall be updated annually on the anniversary date of the on-call agreement, as required by RCW 35.22.620(11)(e).

The quantities provided by the City in the Bid Proposal form are nonbinding estimates which are provided for the sole purpose of bid comparison and to establish the amount of the bid bond and payment & performance bond. The successful bidder is not guaranteed any minimum amount of HVAC and repair work under the on-call agreement, nor is it given the exclusive right to perform such work for the City.

The City of Bellingham is initiating this Request for Proposal (RFP) to solicit proposals from companies interested in operating a shared micromobility service within the City of Bellingham during a one-year pilot program.  Micromobility devices may include electric-assisted bicycles or foot scooters or other similar devices approved by the City.

 

The City’s intent is to use the pilot program to aid the City in developing regulations governing the operation of shared micromobility services within City rights-of-way. Through this RFP the City intends to select one company to operate a shared micromobility service within the City for a one-year pilot period. 

 

Update 3/19/20:

Due to recent events surrounding the Corona Virus and the timing of rolling out a pilot project this summer, the City of Bellingham has decided to delay implementation of the pilot. City is therefore canceling this RFP, with the hopes of re-issuing this fall for implementation in Q1 2021.

Professional engineering services to be performed by the Consultant consist of surveying; facility evaluation; completion of preliminary engineering; and Plan, Specification and Estimate (PS&E) preparation for a bid-ready package for this Wastewater Fund project.

The improvement consists of: Project includes environmental cleanup of two Model Toxics Control Act sites and construction of park facilities on the finished cleanup sites. The cleanup sites sit adjacent to each other on Bellingham Bay and include in-situ solidification of on-site waste, grading of the nearshore, grading of the uplands, installation of an upland capping system, gas collection system, nearshore armoring park utilities, trails, parking facilities and plantings. The in-water portion of the site includes installation of armoring in the nearshore, sediment capping in-water, use of non-ground-penetrating coffer dams, and eelgrass mitigation.

 

Price Range:               $56,000,000 - $61,000,000

 

Plans, specifications, special provisions, basis to be used in comparing bids, proposal and contract can be viewed at the City of Bellingham website (https://cob.procureware.com/) or seen at the Purchasing Office, 210 Lottie Street, Bellingham, Washington, 98225, phone (360) 778-7750. 

 

All proposals must be on the Bid Proposal form provided by the City of Bellingham and must be accompanied by a certified check, cashier's check, cash, money order or bid bond payable to the Finance Director in an amount equal to or exceeding five percent (5%) of the total bid.  No other form of bid security is acceptable. 

 

The right is reserved to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject any and all bids, or to waive irregularities not affecting substantial rights.

The City of Bellingham (“City”) is seeking qualified consulting firms with expertise in mitigation site design, riparian landscape design, surveying, engineering, stream and wetland hydrology/hydraulics, and environmental permitting. The selected firm will assist the City in mitigating for unavoidable environmental impacts within its watersheds. The initial project is designing, permitting, and providing construction support services for the Baker Creek Telegraph mitigation site. The City may also choose to expand the scope of work and extend the contract to include additional mitigation sites and related design and permitting services as needed.

The City of Bellingham reserves the right to amend the terms of this “Request for Qualifications” (RFQ) to circulate various addenda, or to withdraw the RFQ at any time, regardless of how much time and effort consultants have spent on their responses.

The City invites all interested parties to respond to this Request for Qualifications (RFQ) by submitting their Statements of Qualifications (SOQ) relating to this type of project.  Disadvantaged, minority, and women-owned consultant firms are encouraged to respond.  Upon consideration of the submittals, the City will negotiate final terms with the selected party. 

Project Description

The Orchard Drive Extension project, constructed in 2021, resulted in unavoidable impacts to wetlands and buffers. These impacts were originally mitigated through a combination of on-site and off-site mitigation areas. However, ongoing monitoring has determined that the mitigation is only partially meeting permit requirements. As a result, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) has required the City to provide additional mitigation. The City has received preliminary approval from USACE to conduct this additional mitigation at the Baker Creek Telegraph property (Parcel No. 380317044413; see Figure 1).

The selected consultant will design and permit the additional mitigation activities at the Baker Creek Telegraph mitigation site to maximize credit yield. Any mitigation credits generated beyond those required for Orchard Drive Extension may be permitted as advanced mitigation and reserved for future City projects.

The Baker Creek Telegraph mitigation site lies within a shallow valley flanked by forested slopes on the northern and southern boundaries. The valley is traversed by Baker Creek, which flows westward through the site before continuing its southwestward course toward Squalicum Creek. The confluence of Baker Creek with Squalicum Creek lies approximately two miles downstream from the Baker Creek Telegraph parcel. Squalicum Creek, in turn, flows southward and empties into Bellingham Bay, approximately 1.5 miles to the southwest of the confluence.

Hydrological inputs to the Baker Creek Telegraph site are derived from various sources, including direct precipitation, surface runoff from areas upgradient of the site, culverted drainage systems, and the flow of Baker Creek itself. The wetlands and banks along Baker Creek within the Baker

The City of Bellingham Public Works Department provides full engineering review of proposed
public infrastructure construction and public and private stormwater runoff treatment and flow
control designs included in private development projects. The Department uses electronic
permitting and plan review software (Trakit and Bluebeam) and all plan sets are submitted in an
electronic format.
The selected firm will review private development plans to ensure compliance with City of
Bellingham codes and standards. The Consultant performing the work for the City is expected to
be able to provide comprehensive Engineering Development Review services including review of
engineered plans for sewer, water, stormwater and street infrastructure. The firm should have
relevant expertise in civil engineering design and be able to become familiar with City of
Bellingham codes and standards.
The anticipated term of this contract is one year.
Additional services of the same nature and type may be added to the contact at the direction of the
City’s project manager pending availability of other funding and as identified within the City’s
scope of work.

Notice is hereby given that the City of Bellingham is seeking requests for proposals from firms for the disposal of vactor waste and street sweeping waste. These materials are collected by City, County, DOT, and private crews and delivered to 2140 Division Street, Bellingham Washington for dewatering prior to final disposal.

The City of Bellingham is inviting all interested firms to respond to this Printing Services RFP by submitting their electronic proposal. Interested parties may view the solicitation documents on the City of Bellingham website at https://cob.procureware.com/. Questions can be addressed to the Purchasing bids email at Bids@cob.org.

The Purchasing Office at 210 Lottie Street Bellingham, WA 98225 must receive the electronic bids proposals through the City Bid portal ‘’Procureware’’ https://cob.procureware.com/ no later than 11:00 AM on July 31st,  2025. The Electronic sealed bids proposals will be opened and read after the 11:00 AM deadline. The City reserves the right to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject all bids/quotes/proposals or parts of bids/quotes/proposals as may be in the best interest of the City.

Export.Description: The City of Bellingham is soliciting competitive bids for the purpose of establishing a public works contract for ON-CALL MULTIPLE HEARTH INCINERATOR REPAIR. Work will include emergency and nonemergency repair work. All work will be performed on a time and materials basis using the hourly rate(s) and parts and materials markup percentage contained in the contractor’s Bid Proposal, which will be attached to and made a part of the on-call agreement. The term of the on-call agreement will be three (3) years, with the option to extend for one (1) additional year. Over the term of the agreement, the City will identify specific work assignments and request a written quotation from the contractor for the work. The contractor will provide an itemized written quotation for each work assignment using the hourly rate(s) contained in its Bid Proposal. The City will review the Contractor’s quotation and, upon approval, issue a purchase order for the work. Each purchase order will be issued under the on-call agreement and will be subject to its general terms and conditions.

The City of Bellingham (City) is seeking Request for Qualifications (RFQ) to provide Architectural and Engineering services for 43B-2025 Structural repairs of the Commercial Street Parking Garage located at 1300 Commercial Street, Bellingham WA 98225.
The City invites all interested parties to respond to this Request of Qualifications (RFQ) by submitting their qualifications relating to this category of work. All prospective consultants are advised any federally funded project work will be held to federal EEO requirements. Disadvantaged, minority and women-owned consultant firms are encouraged to respond.
The City of Bellingham must receive an electronic copy of the bid documents submittal prior to the date and time specified in the advertisement. All bids must be submitted online at: https://cob.procureware.com/ under the responses tab for this RFQ.
The City requests the electronic copy must be submitted by 11:00am Pacific Time July 22nd, 2025. 
The Consultant performing the work for the City is expected to be able to provide comprehensive architectural and engineering services to support the required structural repairs. Consultants are expected to have previous experience working on commercial parking structures of similar size. The selected consultant will work closely with a City Facilities Project Manager to complete the design. 
Price Range:	$350,000.00 to complete the project
Plans, specifications, special provisions, basis to be used in comparing bids, proposal and contract can be viewed at the City of Bellingham website (https://cob.procureware.com/) or seen at the Purchasing Office, 210 Lottie Street, Bellingham, Washington, 98225, phone (360) 778-7750.  
The right is reserved to postpone making the award for a reasonable length of time, to reject any and all SOQs, or to waive irregularities not affecting substantial rights.
